utterances.speaker: I
utterances.text: Thank you and good evening Mayor Kate and city council members. My name is Scott Eberle. I'm currently a lieutenant, San Police Department. I currently oversee our professional standards unit that oversees our equipment and training needs. I'm here tonight to talk about AB 481 military equipment and our annual annual report. First, a little background. AB 41 was passed in 2021, which requires the governing body, in our case San Fel City Council, to adopt an ordinance approving a military equipment Use Policy for the Funding, acquisition and Use of Military Equipment the government code defines military equipment into 16 separate categories. Out of those categories, Sanfel Police Department only has equipment in seven of the listed categories. To continue using military equipment, the law requires that each year the City Council review the annual report and renew the ordinance it has adopted approving the funding acquisition and use of military equipment. In May of 2022, the City Council adopted Ordinance 2007, adding Chapter 2.52 to the San Rafael Municipal Code to establish the requirements for approval and annual review of our military equipment policy. The San Rafael Police Department Military Equipment Annual Report for calendar year 2023 was attached to the staff report and it included the six required pieces of information. It outlined how the equipment was used and the purpose of its use, any complaints concerning the military equipment, results of any internal audits, costs associated with the equipment and use, full inventory of the equipment we possess, and if we intend to acquire any additional equipment next year. The report details that in most instances we deployed our military equipment for training. However, the San Rafael Police Department did have cause to utilize some equipment in the course of their duties. This was outlined in detail in the annual report, but in summary it included the use of The Marin County Sheriff's Office Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Category 1 six times, otherwise known as a drone, the armored rescue vehicle in category 2 three times, and the less than lethal impact device category 14, once also noted in the report. The San Rafael Police Department did not receive any complaints about using military equipment during the reporting period, nor did any internal audits reveal any policy violations. At the July 17th city council meeting of last year, the Council approved the replacement of 10 aging end of service patrol rifles. I want to report that those 10 rifles were taken to a disposal site where the weapons were melted down and destroyed. The Council also approved the D inventory of eight precision rifles formerly utilized by our precision rifle operators assigned to our SWAT team and purchased two more reliable and accurate rifles and accessories. Those D inventory rifles were also destroyed and not allowed to be repurposed by another law enforcement agency or any member of the public. Besides the above inventory actions, the inventory of the military equipment has not changed in 2023 and it's attached to the annual report. There are no new proposed items for the military equipment list in 2024, except for that we are asking for the replacement of 10 patrol rifles that are at the end of their service life, just as we did last year. As a part of the regulations that govern military equipment use, we provide an opportunity for the public to address any issues, concerns or complaints? The Sanfel Police Department excuse me, Military Equipment use policy number 706 is posted on our website along with information about all the past community meetings that we've held and a link to those videos. On April 17th staff presented of this year, April 17th, 2024, staff presented AB 481 military equipment at the monthly Police Advisory and Accountability Committee meeting. All required elements of the annual report were presented and the committee engaged in useful, inquisitive and productive dialogue. There was one community member who asked a question related to military equipment during public comment and there were no negative comments at the meeting. A summary is provided in my staff report and also available online. There were numerous questions and comments that were received from the PAC members themselves regarding the use of military equipment and this was a good illustration of the productive dialogue that took place. I do list a summary. I can go over a couple of the items that we talked about. One of the questions what I thought was a good question is who performs the internal audits? That's our firearms experts and trainers and our SWAT team leaders. Another question was is there a patrol rifle in every single vehicle? When a patrol car does go in service, there is one patrol rifle per vehicle and the average service life of patrol rifle is about 10 years. At the next PAC meeting on May 22, there was a member of the public who spoke during open time. That member wanted the PAC to be aware that the legislators who wrote the law wanted communities to have input and oversight because military equipment is more frequently used in low income and black and brown communities. The SRPD maintains a feedback tab on SRPD website for the public to share comments of support or concern regarding its military equipment and SRPD did not receive any complaints or concerns on that website. The only change, as I mentioned before, to our military equipment is that we're requesting the replacement of ten outdated patrol rifles. This is part of a multi year phase transition of the Police Department patrol rifle inventory and if approved the old rifles will be destroyed in the same manner the rifles were last year. The cost of replacing Such rifles is $10,446.90. I now want to take a minute and explain why we need the equipment that is listed in the end in the report. The equipment that falls under the definition of military equipment that the San Rafael Police Department has and is used to de escalate violent situations. I want to underscore that the pieces of equipment are used to create time, distance and provide cover to facilitate the time needed to deal with these high risk situations in Every situation, whether violent or not, every officer factors in three things upon initial contact. That's time, distance and cover. Having more time to make decisions gives us more time to weigh options and formulate and discuss contingencies and strategies which create a better opportunity for success and peaceful resolution. The distance to or from any problem will change the tactics and strategy. For example, if a violent subject is within a couple feet of an officer is much different and way more imminent than an officer can stand back 30 to 50 yards and deal with that situation. It'll give the officer more time to react, plan and de escalate. Cover Cover is a term that is used to describe being in a safe area behind ballistic protection. Cover can come from many forms such as an engine block of a vehicle, a large tree or an armored vehicle. All of these pieces of equipment that are outlined in our military equipment inventory list are are necessary to create time, distance and cover. Without these pieces of equipment, the possibility for peaceful outcomes is diminished and the chances for injuries are greatly increased. I do want to underscore again that the San Rafael Police Department prioritizes preventative strategies over reactionary tactics. Some of our preventative strategies that we highlight in the center for Police Department are community policing, crime prevention through environmental design, youth programs, neighborhood watch programs, community outreach and education, partnerships with other agencies, the use of technology such as ALPRs, proactive policing and specialized units, just to name a few. I really wish there would never be a need to deploy any of the equipment that I listed on the Military Equipment Annual Report. But it is better to have it and not need it than to need it and not have it. In conclusion, these pieces of equipment are used to contain the actions of violent endangered subjects and influence their intentions that help us move toward a goal of a peaceful resolution. The equipment that we use and have are available to us is critical for a peaceful resolution for those individuals involved, our officers and the community as a whole. The City Council has three options to consider on this matter tonight. Adopt the resolution renewing the ordinance approving military equipment, Adopt a revised resolution with changes to the military use policy or do not adopt the resolution. It is the recommended action from staff to adopt the resolution renewing the ordinance approving San Rafael Police Department military equipment use poly706 this concludes my presentation and I am available for any questions you may have.
